en: Preface to the *Jie-lu* (Swift Record) of the Orthodox Lineage of Buddhas and Patriarchs from Antiquity to the Present.
Regarding the recorded sayings and deeds of the Buddhas and Patriarchs appearing in the literature of both lands, there are some dozens of collections.

According to the various patriarchs of the Western Heavens, they originated from the lineage of Śākyamuni as transmitted by Sengyou of the Liang dynasty; thus, this constitutes the orthodox tradition of China.
The various records of the *Chuan deng* (Transmission of the Lamp) have been passed down in succession and are fully contained within the *Tripitaka*.

Pervading the entire world for over two thousand six hundred years, they have been transmitted from household to household and recited by every family, enabling our generation to behold the countenances of the ancient sages as clearly as the sun and moon suspended in the midst of heaven;
thus, their grace is indeed vast. Yet, how can one possibly synthesize and condense that which is so grand, profound, and boundless?
How much more so regarding the writings of various families, all of which trace their lineage back to the *Chuan deng lu* (The Record of the Transmission of the Lamp).

Yet, that *Chuan deng lu* ends with Mian Xianjie of the Song dynasty; from that point down to the Yuan, Ming, and up to the present—through seventeen or eighteen successive generations—not even their names have been heard, let alone their clan names, dynasties, or biographical details.
Consequently, while perusing the Tripitaka, I [sought] the source of the Elder of Tiantong at Caoxi...
I have compiled the lineages of the six patriarchs of Shaolin, further incorporating authentic biographical accounts, imperial reigns, monastic seniority, posthumous titles, and dharma heirs.

This work is titled the *Jie-lu* (Abbreviated Record) of the Authentic Lineage from Antiquity to the Present. It is intended so that those who have not yet arrived may trace the stream back to its source, and those who have already entered may unify with the root to direct the branches.
Without needing to search elsewhere, one immediately enters the Treasure Trove of the Dharma King; with a single glance, all is seen.

The perfection of beauty is complete. Our Buddha, when he spoke of contemplating that distant past as if it were this very day, did not intend for a single assembly to remain fixed in its present form;
his intent was solely to cause the True Eye to circulate. This is the purpose of the compiler’s work.

If we calculate from the year our Buddha appeared in the world until he manifested the sign of Nirvana—ninety-seven years after his birth—it was the year of the Ren-shen cycle in the reign of King Mu of the Zhou dynasty. One thousand and ten years later...

Seven hundred years later, twenty generations had passed, reaching Śayananda. This was precisely the *dingmao* year of the Yongping era of Emperor Xiaoming of the Han dynasty in this land, when the teaching first reached China.
From then until one thousand four hundred and seventy years later, twenty-eight generations had passed;
this was the *gengzi* year, the first year of the Putong era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, which coincided with the time Bodhidharma arrived in Jinling. The above accounts are as follows.
The records are quite numerous and are well known to all; thus, they shall not be reproduced here. This is provided merely for the broad learning of future sages.

Written by the junior scholar Xuezhao (Xingshi) on the first day of the New Year in the year of Bingwu, the fifth year of the Kangxi era of the Great Qing, together with verses on the authentic transmission of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and a concise record of ancient and modern cases (including appended *nian* and *song*).
Compiled by the Bhikṣu Guoxing of Western Shu.
The First Patriarch, Master Bodhidharma, was of the Kṣatriya caste. He was the younger son of King Xiangzhi of South India.
He received the Dharma from the twenty-seventh patriarch, Prajñātāra. The patriarch instructed him, saying: "Wait until six years after my passing..."
In the tenth year, he was to go to the land of China to propagate the teachings. [The King] asked, "Are there those in that land who are vessels for the Dharma capable of continuing my lineage?
Will there be obstacles or difficulties after a thousand years have passed? The Patriarch then composed a prophetic verse in advance.

When the Venerable One passed away, the Master began to propagate the teachings in his own country, bringing the six schools back to the orthodox path. When the time came to travel eastward, the King provided a great ship, filled it with various treasures, and personally [escorted him].

Accompanied by his ministers and officials, he escorted [the Master] to the seashore; after three circuits, they reached the South Sea. It was the ninth month of the first year of the Putong era of the Liang dynasty (the Gengzi year).
When the Prefect Xiao Ang submitted a memorial, an imperial decree was issued for the King to receive him in audience.

The King asked, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truth? The Master replied, "Vast emptiness—there is no sage. The King asked, "Who is it that stands before me? The Master replied, "I do not know."
The King did not yet understand his intent, so he crossed the river and went to Wei. He stayed at Shaolin Temple on Mount Song, sitting facing a wall.
After nine years had passed, wishing to return to the Western Heaven, he commanded his disciples to speak of what they had attained.
Dao Fu, Dao Yu, and the nun Zongchi each presented their insights. Finally, Huik’e prostrated himself and stood in his place. The Patriarch said, "You have attained my..."
He then entrusted him with his final instructions, saying: "I came to this land because I saw that the Divine Continent of China possessed the atmosphere of the Mahāyāna.
Now that I have found you, my purpose is fulfilled. Having finished speaking, he sat upright and passed away. A stupa was erected for him at Dinglin Temple on Mount Xiong’er.
This was in the second year of the Datong era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty; three years later, [the Master] encountered Song Yun.
The Matter of the Pamir Mountains. Verse:
"Vast and empty—no sage," he replied to King Liang; Their words did not meet, so they crossed the river in silence.
Even if Shen Guang had offered him an arm, It would cause people for a thousand ages to sigh over his conduct and concealment.
The Second Patriarch, Grand Master Huike, was the son of Lady Ji of Wulao. In his youth, he was widely learned in various texts and reached the utmost refinement in profound principles.
Upon reading the Buddhist sutras, he attained a transcendent realization. He received the tonsure and full ordination at Longmen;

at the age of forty, while in meditative concentration, he saw a deity who told him, "You are about to ascend to the fruit of sainthood. Immediately thereafter, his head began to ache as if pierced by needles. Desiring to seek medical treatment, the deity spoke again:
He said, "This is merely a reshaping of my bones; it is not particularly painful. Because of this, he informed his master. The master examined the crown of his head and saw five peaks protruding.
He told him, "Since the spirits have assisted you, you may go forth to seek the Way. I have heard that Bodhidharma of India has recently arrived at Shaolin;
you should go there to rely upon him. He then went to pay his respects. The Patriarch sat constantly in a meditative posture facing a wall, and no instructions or exhortations were heard.

The Master reflected to himself: "In the past, those who sought the Way would break their bones to extract marrow, pierce their veins to provide sustenance for the hungry, spread their hair to cover the mud, and throw themselves from cliffs to feed tigers.
If the ancients were such as this, what person am I? I have stood in attendance until the break of dawn, with accumulated snow rising above my knees. The Patriarch said:

"The unsurpassed, wondrous Way of all Buddhas has been cultivated with diligent effort through vast eons; it is a path where that which is difficult to practice is practiced, and that which is difficult to endure is endured. How could it be otherwise?"
With little virtue and little wisdom, and with a mind of frivolity and arrogance, he sought to hope for the True Vehicle; his diligent toil was in vain.
Upon hearing this exhortation, the Master severed his arm before the Patriarch. The Patriarch said, "Now that you have severed your arm before me, your seeking is permissible.
You shall be named Huike. The Master said, "My mind is not yet at peace; I beg the Master to pacify my mind. The Patriarch said, "Bring forth your mind, and I will pacify it for you. The Master—
He replied, "I have searched for my mind, but it is utterly unattainable. The Patriarch said, "I have finished settling your mind for you. Thereupon, he attained the Dharma.

In the second year of the Tianping era of the Northern Qi dynasty, he received the transmission of the Dharma from Huicai and went to the capital of Ye, where he practiced the transformation of beings for thirty-four years.

Because Dharma Master Bianhe slandered the district magistrate, Zhai Zhongkan, the master was subjected to legal punishment. Fayu, knowing this to be his prior karma, accepted it with serene composure.
He passed away on the sixteenth day of the third month in the thirteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Great Sui dynasty, at the age of one hundred and seven.
He was buried to the northeast of Cizhou. A verse in praise follows:
Discoursing on the profound and the subtle, his words flowed like a babbling brook; yet upon seeing the Hu monk, he fell silent at once.
At the peak of Duibi, he declared, "I have attained the marrow. From that moment, the stench of worldly fame descended upon the human realm.
The Third Patriarch, Great Master Sengcan, approached the Second Patriarch while still a layman and said: "Your disciple’s body is beset by a chronic wind ailment; I pray you, [grant me the Dharma]."

The Master was performing a ritual for the confession of sins. The Patriarch said, "Bring forth the sin, and I shall confess it for you. After a long while, the practitioner said, "I have searched for the sin, but it is utterly unfindable.

The Patriarch said, "I have finished confessing your sin for you. You should now abide in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. The practitioner asked, "Now that I have met the Master, I already know what is meant by the Sangha;
but I do not yet understand what is called the Buddha and the Dharma. The Patriarch replied, "This very mind is the Buddha; this very mind is the Dharma. The Dharma...
"The Buddha is non-dual; the Jewel of the Sangha is likewise. The man said, "Now I know that the nature of sin does not reside within, without, or in between.
The Patriarch approved this and immediately shaved his hair, saying, "This is my treasure. You should be named Sengcan. He then transmitted the robe and the Dharma, saying:
"Receive my instruction: you should dwell in the deep mountains; you must not yet go forth to transform others. There will be national turmoil.
This is what Prajñātāra predicted in his distant prophecy: 'Though auspicious within the heart, it shall be calamitous without. I have karmic debts from former lives which I must now repay.
Reflect carefully upon this holy record and do not fall into the hardships of the world. Later, when Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty suppressed the teachings, he traveled to Lake Tai.
At Mount Sikong, he remained in profound seclusion for more than ten years, such that no one knew of him.

In the twelfth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, he encountered the śrāmaṇera Daoxin, to whom he transmitted the Dharma. Thereafter, he resided successively at various mountains, including Mount Luofu.

Local officials and commoners followed one another to take refuge in him, and he preached the Dharma to the fourfold assembly. Beneath a great tree, he stood with palms joined in solemnity and passed away. At that time...
On the fifth day of the tenth month of the second year of the Daye era (the Bingyin year) of Emperor Yang of the Sui dynasty, there was a "Inscription on Faith" that circulated in the world:
"My body is entangled in wind-ailments; what crime have I committed? Upon seeing the King of Physicians, the ocean of karma dries up.
Since the arising of sin is non-existent, the mind also vanishes. The Great Master faces me, his lips parted in a smile."
The Fourth Patriarch, Master Daoxin, was surnamed Sima. He resided in Henei, but his father moved to Qizhou. From his youth, the Master yearned for the school of emptiness;

the various gates of liberation were as if already familiar through past habituation. He requested of the Third Patriarch, saying, "I pray that the Venerable One will, out of compassion, grant me the Dharma-gate of liberation.
The Patriarch asked, "Who has bound you? He replied, "No one has bound me. The Patriarch said, "Then why seek liberation?"
Under these words, he attained great enlightenment. He served his master for nine years, maintaining a focused mind without sleep.
Having succeeded to the patriarchal tradition, his side did not touch his mat for sixty years. In the thirteenth year of the Daye era of the Sui dynasty, he led his disciples to Jizhou.

There they encountered a band of rebels surrounding the city, which remained besieged for seventy days without resolution. The multitude was terrified; the Patriarch took pity on them and instructed them to recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
The bandits, seeing from afar between the battlements what appeared to be divine soldiers, said to one another, "There must be extraordinary people within this city," and they subsequently withdrew.
One day, he went to Huangmei and met the Boy, who entrusted him with the dharma-garments.
During the Wude era of Emperor Gaozu of the Tang, he went to Mount Poutou to seek out Lanrong and lived in seclusion there; disciples flocked to him, and Emperor Taizong heard of his fame.

The Master’s conduct was rooted in the Way and its Virtue. He declined three imperial summons. The Emperor grew angry and issued an edict to bring his head. When the messenger arrived, the Master extended his neck toward the blade; his countenance remained unchanged.
The messenger returned and reported this, and Emperor Taizong’s admiration and reverence for him increased all the more.

He passed away on the fourth day of the intercalary ninth month in the second year of the Yonghui era (751 CE) during the reign of Emperor Gaozong of the Tang dynasty. He was seventy-two years old. His stupa was erected at Mount Dong. A verse in his praise follows:
Exhausting all diligence, one counts the sands of the ocean; Without a rope, one binds oneself, eyes clouded by hemp.
By chance, where needle and eye meet, A shift in the mechanism of the line brings one home.
The Fifth Patriarch, Master Hongren of Huangmei, was a son of the Zhou clan from Qizhou. Previously, he had been a woodcutter at Mount Poutu.

The monk Songdao constantly requested the Dharma from the Fourth Patriarch. The Patriarch said, "You are now old; even if you were to hear [the teaching], would you be able to transform others extensively?
If you should come again, I may wait for you. Thereupon, he went to walk by the water's edge and saw a woman washing clothes. He bowed to her and asked for lodging.
The woman nodded her head in consent, and he immediately turned his staff and departed. When the woman returned home, she became pregnant. Her father—
His mother, being wicked, cast him out. Having nowhere to turn, he took up employment spinning at the foot of a public hall.
Later, he fathered a son; deeming this an ill omen, she abandoned him in a harbor. The next day, as he was wading upstream, his physical form appeared exceptionally radiant.
Those who saw him were struck with wonder. They raised him until he reached the age of childhood. Once, a strange monk sighed and said, "This boy lacks seven of the marks [of a Great Man]."
Upon reaching the Tathāgata, one day while traveling on the road at Huangmei, he encountered the Fourth Patriarch, who asked, "What is your surname?
He replied, "I have a surname, but it is not an ordinary surname. The Patriarch asked, "What is this surname? He replied, "It is Buddha-nature. The Patriarch asked, "Do you have no surname?
He replied, "Because its nature is emptiness, it has none. The Patriarch silently recognized that he was a vessel for the Dharma and immediately dispatched an attendant to his mother.
He requested to leave the household life. His mother, due to their past karmic connection, showed no sign of reluctance and granted his request.
Thereupon, he received the Dharma and propagated the Way at Huangmei. During the Xianheng era, he transmitted the Dharma to Lu Neng.

He passed away in the second year of Shangyuan (the year of Yihai) during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, at the age of seventy-four. His posthumous title was Daman. Thirteen people succeeded him in the Dharma. Verse:
Lineage and clan are both forgotten; names are likewise empty. Realizing there is nothing to rely upon, one abides within the circle of the center.
On Mount Pòtóu, a thousand trees stand; day and night, the wind whistles through ten thousand apertures.
The Great Master Huineng of the Sixth Patriarch was surnamed Lú. He was originally a native of Fanyáng. His father was Héngtāo, and his mother was née Lǐ.

He was transferred to Xinzhou in Nanhai. Moved by a miraculous dream, she conceived and carried him for six years before giving birth. At the age of three, he lost his father; his mother observed the period of mourning and nurtured him with her own hands.
Upon reaching adulthood, his family was poor, so he provided for them by gathering firewood. One day, he was carrying firewood to the market.
Hearing a guest reciting the sutras, he attained a realization. He went directly to Huangmei. The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from?

He replied, "I have come from Lingnan. The Patriarch said, "What do you seek? He replied, "I only seek to become a Buddha. The Patriarch said, "The people of Lingnan have no Buddha-nature; how can they possibly become Buddhas?
He replied, "People may indeed be from the north or the south, but how could the Buddha-nature be like that? The Patriarch said, "This barbarian has a most excellent root-nature."

Lì went to the fodder barn and then entered the mortar house, where he performed manual labor for eight months. The Patriarch, knowing that the time for the transmission had arrived, ordered his disciples to each write a verse.
He declared that if the meaning and phrasing were in perfect accord, he would transmit both the robe and the Dharma.

Of the more than seven hundred monks in the assembly, all venerated Shenxiu and had him write his verse upon the wall; the Master (Huineng) followed suit and composed one as well. One day, the Patriarch went secretly to the mortar house...
Fang saw the Master carrying a stone on his waist and pounding rice. He asked, "Is the rice cooked yet? The Master replied, "The rice has been cooked for a long time; it only lacks the sifting.
The Patriarch struck the mortar three times with his staff, whereupon the Master immediately beat the drum three times and entered the room.

The Patriarch entrusted him with the lineage and transmission from the beginning, saying, "In the past, when Bodhidharma first arrived, people did not believe him. Therefore, he transmitted the robe as a token of faith."
"Now that your faith is matured, the robe is merely a source of contention. Cease this; do not transmit it. Having finished speaking, the Master knelt and received [the robe].
He then asked, "Where will you go? The Patriarch replied, "When I meet Hui, I shall stop; when I encounter Hui, I shall hide. That night he departed and remained hidden between Huaiji and Sihuai.
In the first year of the Yifeng era, he arrived at Caoxi, where he triggered an awakening through the incident of the wind and the banner.
Yinzong thereupon extensively expounded the Dharma-gate of Dongshan. Although Emperor Zhongzong repeatedly issued imperial edicts summoning him, he did not go.

He entered nirvana on the second day of the eighth month of the second year of the Xiāntián era (the *guichǒu* year), at the age of seventy-six. His stupa was erected at Caoxī, and he was posthumously titled Dàjiàn.
Forty-two individuals succeeded him in the Dharma. Verse:
To say that "nothingness is the original state" is already too much; one's whole body finds it difficult to emerge from the bag of Huangmei.
When the point of the awl pierces through, one stands beyond the wind and the banner; a single drop of Caoxi opens the five petals.
The First Patriarch, Chan Master Huairang of Nanyue, was born on the Buddha’s Birthday in the third year of the Yifeng era of Emperor Gaozong. His spiritual resonance...
Extraordinary auspicious signs appeared in the celestial phenomena. The Grand Astrologer reported this to the Emperor, who issued an edict to personally comfort the master’s family.
At fifteen, he received the full precepts (*upasampadā*). Together with Tanran, he went to pay his respects to National Teacher Huian. Huian ordered him to go to Caoxi to see the Sixth Patriarch.
The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Mount Song. The Patriarch said, "What thing comes in such a manner? The Master was speechless. Thus, eight years passed.
Zai suddenly attained a realization. He then said to the Patriarch, "I have reached a point of understanding.
The Patriarch asked, "How so? The Master replied, "To describe it as a single thing is not correct. The Patriarch asked, "Can it still be cultivated and realized?
The Master replied, "Cultivation and realization are not non-existent; however, it cannot be defiled. The Patriarch said, "This very state of being undefiled is that which all Buddhas protect."
[The Master] said, "Nian, since you are thus, I am also thus. The Indian Prajñātāra prophesied: 'From beneath your feet shall emerge a colt that will trample the people of the world to death;
you must not preach the Buddha-dharma too soon. After the Master attained the Dharma, he served his Patriarch for another fifteen years.
In the second year of the Tiangong era, he went to Mount Heng and resided at Prajñā Monastery. During the Kaiyuan period, he attained [realization]."
The śramaṇa Daoyi transmitted the Dharma. He entered nirvāṇa on the eleventh day of the eighth month in the third year of the Tiānbǎo era of Emperor Xuánzōng of the Táng dynasty.
His posthumous title was Dàhuì (Great Wisdom). Nine persons succeeded him in the Dharma. Verse:
What thing comes thus? The movement of Heaven is discordant and the flowers do not bloom;
When the cold reaches its peak, piercing to the very bone, The spring wind drags green across the mossy ground.
The Second Patriarch, Chan Master Mazu Daoyi, was the son of the Ma family in Shifang County, Hanzhou, Sichuan. His appearance...
His appearance was extraordinary and imposing. He walked like an ox and gazed like a tiger; he could extend his tongue past his nose, and his feet possessed two wheels.

He left home at the Luohan Temple in his native city. After receiving full ordination, during the Kaiyuan era, he practiced meditative concentration on Mount Heng. Master Rang recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma.
The Master asked, "What is the purpose of sitting in meditation? Dongshan Liangjie replied, "To become a Buddha. Liangjie then took a brick and began to grind it on a stone in front of the hermitage.
The Master asked, "What are you grinding that for? Liangjie said, "I am grinding it to make a mirror. The Master said, "How can grinding a brick produce a mirror?
Liangjie said, "If grinding a brick cannot produce a mirror, how can sitting in meditation produce a Buddha? The Master asked, "Then what should be done?"
This was indeed so. Rang said, "It is like an ox pulling a cart. If the cart does not move, one may strike the cart; one may also strike the ox. The Master had no reply.
Rang showed him a verse, saying: "The ground of the mind contains all seeds; When it meets with moisture, they all sprout. The flower of samādhi is formless;

What is there to destroy, and what is there to achieve? Having received this instruction, the Master’s mind was suddenly enlightened. He departed to reside in Jiangxi. Upon entering [the community], he...

He had one hundred and thirty-nine disciples in his quarters. Observing that students were left without support in their vigor and without a place of refuge in their old age, he established monastic communities (*conglin*) to govern them.
On the first day of the second month in the fourth year of the Zhenyuan era of the Tang Emperor Dezong, he entered *parinirvāṇa*.
His worldly age was eighty; he was posthumously titled Daji (Great Quiescence). One hundred and thirty-nine people succeeded him in the Dharma. Verse:
Trampling upon living beings, the celestial steed’s colt; Grinding a tile is not a mirror—already he knew this, and clearly realized that flowers have no form.
The prophecy was fulfilled in the Western Heaven by more than one hundred thousand [monks].
The Third Patriarch, Chan Master Baizhang Huaihai of Fuzhou, was a native of the Wang family in Changle. In his youth, he mastered the Three Studies.
Having long relied upon Mazu Daishi, while standing in attendance, he saw a flock of wild ducks fly past.
The Patriarch asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "Wild ducks. The Patriarch asked, "Where have they gone? The Master replied, "They have flown away.
The Patriarch then pinched the Master’s nose, causing him to cry out in pain. The Patriarch said, "And you say they have flown away? At these words, the Master attained realization. Subsequently...

He passed away on the seventh day of the first month in the ninth year of the Yuanhe era of Emperor Xianzong of the Tang dynasty. Fifteen people succeeded him in the Dharma. His posthumous title was "Dazhi" (Great Wisdom). Verse:
A flock of wild ducks flies toward the sky; Suddenly pulled back by the nose, they are dragged like horse winnowing baskets.
Rolling up their mats, they return to the quarters, displaying their ugly forms. From the beginning, this has been both laughable and pitiable.
The Fourth Generation Master Huangbo Xiyun was a native of Min. A protrusion rose upon his forehead, and his disposition was serene and refined. He went to study under [Master Mazu].
When Mazu passed away, Baizhang was dwelling beside his stupa. He then inquired about the phrase by which Mazu had attained realization during his lifetime.
Baizhang recounted the circumstances of Mazu’s second visit, saying, "In the past, when I was struck by Master Mazu with a single shout, my ears were deaf for three days.
Upon hearing this account, the Master involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Baizhang said, "In the future, you must not become a successor."
"Does Mazu go? The Master said, "Not so. Today, because you raised this matter, I have been able to see the great function of Mazu’s spiritual power.
However, I do not recognize Mazu; if I were to accept him as my teacher, my descendants would later lose their own selves. The Elder said, "So it is, so it is.
When one's insight is equal to the teacher's, it diminishes the teacher's virtue by half; only when one's insight surpasses the teacher's is one fit to receive the transmission. My son.
He possessed a vision that far surpassed his teacher. One day, the Master asked him, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from beneath Mount Daxiong to gather mushrooms.
The Master said, "Did you see a tiger? The Master made a tiger's roar. The Master raised his axe and made a gesture of hacking.
The Master struck the Master with a slap. The Master laughed heartily and departed. Upon returning, he ascended the hall and said, "Beneath Mount Daxiong, there is a great..."
"O insects! You all must watch carefully. The old man Baizhang has today personally swallowed one mouthful.
He resided at Huangbo Mountain in Hongzhou and had thirty-three successors who inherited his Dharma.
He passed away during the Dazhong era of the Tang Emperor Xuanzong and was posthumously titled Duanji. Verse:"
Marquis Wu’s loyalty and righteousness shook his family and state; even after death, he still startled Sima [Yan].
Exhausting his sincere heart to support the altars of state, the hero’s name and surname resound through the ages. The Fifth Generation:
Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Nanhua, Caozhou. A native of the Xing clan, he was burdened from childhood with a spirit that transcended the mundane world.
With this resolve, he shaved his head and received full ordination, immediately entering the service of Huangbo. His practice was singularly pure. At that time, Muzhou served as the head seat;
he urged [Xuedou] to ask Huangbo, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Huangbo struck him. He asked this three times and was struck three times.
He then took leave of Huangbo and went to visit Dayu. Dayu asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Huangbo. Dayu—
[The Master] said, "What words did Huangbo have? The Master recounted the previous conversation and added, "I do not know whether I am at fault or not.
Wuzhuo said, "Huangbo was so compassionate as to exhaust you to the very limit, yet you still seek out his faults.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "So it turns out that Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much after all. Wuzhuo grabbed him and said, "This bed-wetting boy!"
"Devil child! Just now you asked whether there was a fault or not; now you say that the Buddha-dharma is not much.
What principle have you seen? Speak quickly, speak quickly! The Master struck Danyuan three times under the ribs.
Danyuan pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo; it has nothing to do with me. The Master returned to Huangbo and related the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "Danyuan..."
"This old fellow is too talkative; wait until he comes, and I will give him a thorough beating. The Master said, "What do you mean by 'wait until he comes'?
I shall beat him right now! He then slapped him. Baizhang said, "This madman has come here to pull at a tiger's whiskers.
The Master then shouted. Baizhang said, "Attendant, lead this madman away to attend the hall. Later, he resided at Linji in Zhenzhou, where his disciples gathered like clouds.

In his assembly, he established the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials (*sanxuan san-yao*), employing the examination of guest and host to test his students. Later, he resided at Xinghua Temple in Daming Prefecture.
Twenty-four people succeeded to his Dharma. He passed away on the fourth month of the *dinghai* year, the eighth year of the Xian Tong era of Emperor Yizong of the Tang dynasty.
His posthumous title was Huizhao. Verse:
Worn-out rush sandals are not of good use; what is the intent behind inciting others to eat the staff?
When Gaoyuan applies moxibustion to a painful spot, he brings disaster upon his descendants.
The Sixth Generation: Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian. Initially, he served as an attendant to Linji. Later, he was in the assembly of Sansheng.
He served as the head seat (śrāmaṇera). He once said, "I traveled on foot through the south until I was struck by a staff;
I have never encountered a single person who truly understands the Buddha-dharma. When Master Sheng heard this, he asked, "What kind of eye do you possess to speak in such a manner?
The Master then gave a shout. Sheng said, "It must be you who possesses it. Later, he became the administrator (karmadāna) at Dajue Temple. One day...
Rizhao said, "I have heard that you traveled south on pilgrimage and, upon encountering a staff once, never managed to strike anyone who truly understands the Buddha-dharma.
On what basis do you speak in such a manner? The Master then shouted; Rizhao struck him. The Master shouted again;
Rizhao struck him again. The next day, as the Master was passing by the Dharma Hall, Rizhao called out to the Hall Superintendent, "I—"
"I suspect you of those two shouts yesterday. The Master shouted again. Yuanjue hit him once more. The Master shouted again. Yuanjue hit him yet again.
The Master said, "I learned a 'host and guest' phrase from my elder brother, Sanxing, but it has been completely dismantled by you, elder brother.
I pray that you will grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and happiness. Yuanjue said, "You blind fellow! Come here!"

He admitted his failure. [Linji] stripped him of his patched robe and beat him soundly. Suddenly, upon these words, he realized the principle behind how his late master Linji had received the staff from Huangbo.
He went forth to reside at Xinghua, and on the day of opening the hall, he offered incense, saying:
This incense stick was originally intended for my elder brother, Master Sansheng; yet Sansheng is too remote for me. It was originally intended for my elder brother, Master Dajue;

yet Dajue is too distant for me. It is better that I offer it to my late teacher, Linji. During the reign of Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang, he was summoned by imperial decree and granted the purple robe.
Among the five who succeeded his Dharma, he passed away in the second year of Tongguang, the year of Yiyou (925 CE), and was posthumously titled Guangji.
Fierce frost and cold snow press upon the plum blossoms; Touched by the spring breeze, their eyes open in a smile.
He does not allow the falling petals to drift away with the water, Fearing they might startle the mournful cries of the night monkeys in the Ba Gorges.
The Seventh Patriarch, Chan Master Huiyong of Nanyuan, was a native of Hebei. Having received the Dharma from Xinghua, he resided at Nan [Mountain] in Ruzhou.
At Bao Ying Temple in Chan, the Master ascended the hall and said: "Upon this lump of red flesh, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
At that time, a monk asked, "Is it not you, Master, who said: 'Upon this lump of red flesh, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high'?

The Master replied, "Yes. The monk overturned the meditation seat. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow making such a mess! As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and drove him out. Later, [five...]
He passed away in the second year of the Guangshun era (Renzi) of Emperor Taizu of the Later Zhou. He had two successors in the Dharma lineage. Verse:
The true person of no station is a bare lump of flesh; From of old, its nostrils have reached across the vast heavens.
When the occasion arises, he turns the pivot of a thousand-jin weight; He shoots straight toward the realm beyond Vipaśyin Buddha.
The Eighth Patriarch, Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue, was a native of the Liu family in Yuhang. Having failed in his first attempt at the imperial examinations, he left the household life.
He initially studied under Jingqing and subsequently visited Nanyuan. Nanyuan asked, "How do you interpret a staff-blow from the South?
The Master replied, "I interpret it as something extraordinary. The Master then asked in turn, "How do you interpret a staff-blow here in this monastery, Reverend?"
The Master held up his staff and said, "Under the blow of the staff is the patience of non-arising; when facing the critical moment, one does not see the teacher.

At these words, the Master attained a great realization of the profound principle. Later, while fleeing from the chaos, he was invited by the Magistrate Li of Yingzhou to give a formal discourse, in which he said: "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs..."
"This resembles the mechanism of an iron ox: when it departs, it is sealed; when it stays, it is broken. As for neither departing nor staying—is it the seal itself, or is it not the seal?
At that moment, the Elder Lupi stepped forward and said, "I possess the mechanism of the iron ox; I request the Master not to apply the seal.
The Master replied, "You who are accustomed to hooking whales and leviathans in the vast depths, yet sigh over the leap of a frog."

Later, because Song Hou, the Grand Master of Ruizhou, donated his residence to become a temple, he invited the Master to serve as its abbot. In the first year of the Guangshun era of the Zhou dynasty, he again took charge of Fengxue.

The Master was born on the twelfth month of the Bingchen year, the third year of the Qianning era of Emperor Zhaozong of the Tang dynasty, and passed away during the Kaifeng era of Emperor Taizu of the Song dynasty.

On the Mid-Autumn Day of the sixth year of the Baoyu era, the year of Guiyou (1093), he ascended the seat, recited a verse, and passed away. His stupa was enshrined on the western bank of the stream in front of the temple.
There were four successors to his Dharma lineage. Verse:
Under the staff, the patience of non-arising; at the moment of action, the teacher is not seen.
Treading over the moon in the vast ocean, he releases the mechanism of the iron ox.
Leaping over the three surges of the Yu Gate, he yet sighs at the frog’s pace as it wades through the sand and mud.
The Ninth Patriarch, Chan Master Shengnian of Mount Shou in Xiang County, was born of the Di clan of Lai Prefecture.
He traveled extensively among monastic assemblies, privately reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*. Later, he relied upon Fengxue as the *zhiké* (guest prefect).
While standing in attendance, Fengxue shed tears and told him, "It is unfortunate that the Way of Linji is about to fall to the ground by my time. The Master replied, "I observe this assembly..."
"Is there no one at all? Xue said, "Those who are clever and intelligent are many; those who see their own nature are few. The Master asked, "What about someone like me?
Xue said, "Although I have long looked forward to you, I fear you may become attached to this scripture and be unable to let it go.
The Master said, "This is also a matter of concern; I wish to hear its essential point. Xue then ascended the hall and raised the theme of the World-Honored One’s blue-lotus eyes.
He looked around at the great assembly and said, "Tell me, what was it he spoke of? If you say he spoke without speaking, that would be to bury the former sages.
So tell me, what did he speak of? The Master then shook his sleeves and went down; Xue threw down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
An attendant monk asked, "Why did Nian Fahua not give a reply to the Master? Xue said, "Nian Fahua understood."
The next day, he went up with the head monk Zhen to pay his respects. Xue said, "What is the Buddha’s 'speaking that which is not spoken'?
Zhen said, "A magpie calls from the top of the tree. The Master said, "Expressing oneself through movement reveals the ancient path; one does not fall into the trap of silent stillness."
Xue said to Zhen, "Why do you perform so much 'foolish merit'? Why do you not contemplate the words of the *Lotus Sūtra*?

Later, while residing at Shoushan, he greatly propagated the Way of Linji. On the fourth day of the twelfth month of the third year of the Chunhua era (the Renchen year) of Emperor Taizong’s reign in the Song dynasty, he ascended the seat and said:
"This year I am sixty-seven; old age and illness pass the days as they come. This year..."
He recorded events for the coming year, noting: "In the coming year, record this very day. When that time arrived, he sat peacefully and passed away.
His remains were cremated, and his *śarīra* relics were collected; a stupa was erected at his original mountain seat. Seventeen people succeeded him in the Dharma. A verse:
Laying Aside the *Lotus Sūtra*, He Ascends the Hall: The blue-lotus eyes blink, leaving nothing to be accepted;
Returning, he sits loftily at Shoushan Temple; Clear moon and pure wind fill the Great Tang.
The Tenth Generation Master, Fenyang Wude Shenxiao, was the son of the Yu clan of Taiyuan. From his youth, he possessed great ambition. He studied under Master Zong...
Over seventy people stayed there overnight. Later, he visited Shoushan and asked, "What is the meaning of Baizhang’s folding of his mat?

Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed. He asked, "What about your own intention, Master? Shoushan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. At these words, he attained great enlightenment.
Rising from his prostrations, he said, "The moon in the empty realm of the ten thousand ages’ green pool—though one searches for it again and again..."

One should know that this begins with a loud shout. Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that led you to accept [the invitation] so readily? He replied, "This is precisely where I shall lay down my life.
I have served with great toil for a very long time; though I was invited eight times, both before and after, to preside over famous monasteries, I remained firm in my refusal and did not go."
In the fourth year of the Chunhua era, Shoushan entered nirvana. His dharma-brother Qichong led more than a thousand monastics and laypeople from the Xidao region;

they pushed open the door and entered, entreating him, saying: "The great matter of the Buddha-dharma is not a minor point such as retiring in tranquility. Fengxue feared he would fulfill the prophecy, and we worried that the fundamental teaching would fall into extinction.
Fortunately, there was our former master; now that the former master has passed away, you alone have the strength to shoulder the burden of the Tathāgata."
"A Great Dharma Master—how could he wish to sleep soundly at such a time? The Master started up in alarm, grasped Cōng’s hand, and said, "If it were not for you, I would never have heard these words.

He then went forth to the Taizi Yuan (Prince’s Court) in Fenzhou, where he composed the *Shizhi tongzhen* (Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality) to distinguish between the true and the false among the clergy.

Later, Lord Li of Longde Prefecture, who had long been acquainted with the Master, invited him to reside at Chengtian Monastery; though the Lord visited several times, the Master did not rise from his seat. The messenger...

[The master] was punished. Later, [a monk] arrived and said, "Not so; there is only death. The Master ordered food to be prepared, his travel gear to be readied, and announced to the assembly, "The old monk is departing.
Who can follow me? At that time, several monks did not grasp the meaning. An attendant came forward and said, "I can follow you, Master;
I shall go wherever you go. The Master said, "You indeed can follow the old monk," and then he looked back at his servant.
He said, "I shall depart first," and as he set down his chopsticks, he passed away. His attendant also passed away standing by his side.

He lived for seventy-eight years and sat in meditation for fifty-six summers. Sixteen people succeeded him in the Dharma. This was the year of the Jiazi cycle, the first year of the Tiānshèng era of Emperor Rénzōng of the Song dynasty.
His *śarīra* were collected and a stupa was erected at the temple. A verse:
The dragon-sleeve sweeps open to reveal the great capacity; the lunar disc is dredged until nothing remains.
The trident-heads and halberds of the Three Mysteries clear the universe; killing and giving life are distinct, with not a thread of concealment.
The eleventh-generation Master Ciming Chuyuan of Shishuang was a native of the Li clan from Qingxiang in Quanzhou. (2)
At twelve, he left the household life. His mother was of virtuous conduct and sent him to travel abroad. At the Spring of Great Folly Valley, he joined a group to visit Fenyang.

After two years had passed, he was not permitted to enter the inner quarters; whenever he saw [the Master], he would invariably scold and revile him. One day, he complained, saying: "Since arriving at this Dharma seat, I have received no instruction.
I reflect that time passes swiftly, yet my own task remains unclarified. I feel I have failed and brought disgrace upon my renunciation of the world."
Before he had finished speaking, Wufeng scolded him, saying, "This is a false teacher who dares to deceive me! He raised his staff to drive him away.

As the master (Zhaozhou) was about to intervene to rescue him, Wufeng covered his mouth. Thereupon, the master attained great enlightenment and said, "Now I know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiment."

After serving for seven years, he took his leave and went to reside at Shishuang in Tanzhou. Throughout his life, the Master engaged with others through the principle of non-obstruction in all things;
neither ordinary people nor sages could fathom him. While sitting in meditation in his room, he would place a knife horizontally across a water basin, with a straw sandal set beside it.
He had his disciples offer responses to test their realization of the pivotal moment of the Dharma. Seventy-eight people attained the Dharma.

He entered nirvana on the first day of the Lantern Festival in the year of Xinsi (1041), the first year of the Qingli era of Emperor Renzong of the Song dynasty. His stupa was enshrined at Shishuang. [His] verse:
Drifting through the years to attain freedom, A single banner is carried by the wind to Yangzhou.
Within the chamber, he brandishes a sharp, hair-piercing blade: "Retribution for grievance, and vengeance for enmity.
The Twelfth Generation: Chan Master Yangqi Fanghui. He was the son of the Cold family in Yichun, Yuanzhou. From a young age, he was alert and quick-witted.
He did not devote himself to the brush or inkstone. Upon leaving the household life, whenever he read the scriptures, he would immediately achieve a profound spiritual realization.
He attended on Ciming and took charge of the affairs of the monastery. Every time he went to consult Ciming, Ciming would say, "The affairs of the storehouse are many; go for now.

On another day when he asked again, Ciming said, "In the future, when your disciples and grand-disciples fill the world, what need will there be for such haste? One day, as Ciming went out, the Master followed him along a narrow path.

He grabbed him and said, "This old fellow, you must explain this to me today; if you do not, I will beat you away. On the following day, Ming said, "Abbot, if you understand such matters, then let it be.

Before he had finished speaking, the Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself on the ground. The next day, when Ming ascended the hall, the Master came forward and asked, "When the dark birds warble their cries, leaving the clouds to enter the turbulent winds—what then?
Ming replied: "Ox-head and Tiger-mouth, The ten thousand peaks are cold and desolate. If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the bright moon in the sky."
"I am walking through the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village. The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle.
He then posed a question. Ming gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout! Ming shouted again. The Master also shouted. Ming shouted twice in succession. The Master bowed.
Ming said, "This matter can only be taken up by one who is a true person. The Master shook his sleeves and departed. Later, he resided at Yang.
Qiji once used the phrases regarding the "Vajra Ring" and the "Tornate Thorn" to examine and discern practitioners from all quarters.

He passed away in the *bingxu* year, the first year of the Rensong era of the Song dynasty (1046 CE). His stupa was erected at his native mountain. He had fourteen successors who inherited the Dharma. [Verse:]
Busily attending to the affairs of the monastery, he did not shrink from toil;

Upon a three-legged lame donkey, he played with its high-hoofed feet, Riding backward straight up to the summit of Mount Sumeru, Where the great earth, mountains, and rivers rested upon a single hair-tip.
The Thirteenth Generation: Chan Master Baoyun Shouduan. A native of the Ge clan from Hengyang, he served under the brush [studied calligraphy] in his youth. Upon reaching maturity...
Dependent upon Cha-ling Yu, he went to attend Yang-ch'i. Yang-ch'i asked, "Who is your preceptor? He replied, "The Venerable Cha-ling Yu.
Yang-ch'i said, "I have heard that he had an awakening after falling while crossing a bridge; he composed a verse about it that was truly extraordinary. Can you remember it?"
The Master recited a verse; Qiji smiled and rose from his seat. The Master was startled. Throughout the night, Qiji remained clear-minded and alert. At dawn, the Master questioned him about it.
Qiji said, "Did you see those who were beating the *ou-no* (exorcist puppets) yesterday? He replied, "I saw them. Qiji said, "In this matter, you are one step behind them.
The Master was again struck with wonder and asked, "What is the meaning of this? Qiji said, "They love to be laughed at; you fear being laughed at."
The Master attained great enlightenment upon hearing these words. He served as an attendant for a long time before taking leave to travel to Mount Lu.

Zen Master Net of Yuan Tong appointed him to preside over Chengtian Temple, where his reputation became widely renowned. He subsequently moved to Fahua, Longmen, Xinghua, and Haihui; wherever he went, the assembly gathered like clouds.
He passed away in the Bingxu year, the fifth year of the Xining era of Emperor Shenzong of the Song dynasty, at the age of forty-eight. His stupa was erected.
At Baiyun in Shuzhou, there were twelve dharma heirs who received his transmission. A verse says:
I have secretly acquired Jīvaka’s divine medical arts; His entire being is filled with the heart of a living person.
True prescriptions and false medicines must prove efficacious; In the end, they cannot deceive those within.
The Fourteenth Patriarch, Zen Master Fayan of Wuzu in Qizhou, was a native of the Deng clan from Mianzhou.
At the age of thirty-five, he first shaved his head and received full ordination. He initially visited Fushan, who sent him to Baiyun.

There, he was asked about the story of Nanyuan’s "mani jewel," and Baiyun rebuked him. The Master attained realization and presented this verse: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; I join my palms..."

Yun instructed him to inquire of his grandfather. Several times Yun purchased goods from him and then sold them back to him himself. As neighbors, they shared the pure breeze among their pines and bamboo.
Yun then gave him formal approval (*inka*) and appointed him to oversee the mill. One day Yun said, "There were several Zen practitioners who came from Mount Lu; all of them had attained realization.
When I asked them to speak, they were able to explain with proper justification. When I presented them with kōans (*in'en*), they also understood them clearly."
[The Master] said, "He has attained it. Even though he can give instructions and speak with authority, he is simply not yet there. The Master then became doubtful and reflected to himself:
"Since he has awakened, understood clearly, and can explain it, how is it that he is still 'not yet there'? After investigating this for many days, he suddenly attained realization.
All that he had previously cherished was cast aside at once. He went to see Baiyun, who greeted him by dancing and leaping about. Later, the Master said:
Because of this, I broke into a cold sweat all over my body; thus, I clearly attained the pure breeze of a thousand autumns.
He passed away in the third year of the Chongning era of Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty. Twenty-three people succeeded him in the Dharma. Verse:
"Only when you casually recognize the maṇi jewel, And crush its radiance, will it become naturally so.
After one moment of pure, cold sweat, Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves.
The Fifteenth Generation Chan Master Zhaojue Keler was a native of the Luo family from Pengzhou. As a child, he could memorize a thousand characters a day.
He said, "Once, while wandering through Miaoji Temple, I saw a Buddhist scripture. After reading it three times, I felt a sense of profound longing, as if I had recovered an old possession.

I thought to myself, 'I am surely a śramaṇa from a past life. Having left the household life to pursue the study of the teachings, I abandoned my reliance on the white clouds to serve as an attendant.

One day, a provincial official came to the Patriarch to inquire about the Way. The Patriarch asked, 'Did you, the Investigating Judge, read any light erotic poetry in your youth? There are two lines that are quite—"*
[They were] close together. [The Master] called out "Xiaoyu" repeatedly, though there was no business at all;

he simply wanted the husband to recognize the voice. The attendant responded, "Yes, sir. The Patriarch said, "Be careful. While the Master was standing in attendance, he asked, "Does the Provincial Commissioner understand?
The Patriarch said, "He only recognizes the voice. The Master said, "It is simply that the husband wants to recognize the voice. Since he recognizes the voice, why does he not [understand]?"
"Yes. The Patriarch asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? [Baizhang] replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.
The Master suddenly attained realization; he hurriedly went outside and saw a chicken fly onto the railing, flap its wings, and crow. He then said, "Is this not sound?"
He then presented a verse, saying: "The golden duck has consumed the incense within the brocade curtains; Amidst the strains of pipes and songs, I am supported home by a drunkard.
This episode of youthful elegance— Only the beloved knows it alone. The Patriarch then announced to the senior monks of the mountain:

My attendant attained realization through Zen meditation. He went forth to reside at Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu, where he was commissioned by imperial decree to propagate the Dharma in several locations and repeatedly received imperial honors and gifts.
On the day of Jiyou in the eighth month of the fifth year of the Shaoxing era of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty, he wrote a verse, set down his writing brush, and passed away.

The relics from the cremation were five-colored; they were enshrined in a stupa at his home temple, and he was posthumously titled "True Enlightenment" (Zhenguang). Seventy-six people succeeded him in the Dharma.
To repeatedly call for "Little Jade" (Xiaoyu) with no other intent— Try asking the husband of the donor, do you understand?
Even if you recognize the sound, it is not yet it. The rooster’s cry is exquisite; one recognizes Cao E.
The sixteenth-generation Chan Master Shao Long of Huqiu was a native of Hanshan in Hezhou. He left home at the age of nine. Upon reaching adulthood, he traveled to study under various masters;
he first visited Changlu and later met Foguo. One day, while entering the master’s room for instruction, Foguo asked him:
"When seeing the very act of seeing, that seeing is not [ordinary] seeing. Seeing is already detached from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. Raising his fist, Foguo asked, "Do you see it?"
The Master said, "I see. Wuzhuo said, "Placing a head atop a head. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization of the truth. Guo scolded him, saying, "What have you seen?
The Master replied, "Though the bamboos are dense, they do not hinder the flowing water from passing through. Guo then approved of him.

Someone asked, "If Master Long Zang’s gentle disposition is such as this, how can he be of any use? Wuzhuo said, "He is but a sleeping tiger. Later, the Prefectural Governor, Lord Li Guang... [text ends]
Yan resided at Zhangjiao. Subsequently, he moved to Huqiu in Pingjiang, where his Way became greatly manifest.

On the sixth day of the fifth month in the sixth year of the Shaoxing era of Emperor Gaozong of the Song dynasty (the Bingchen year), he manifested parinirvāṇa. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the southwest of the temple. He had one successor in the Dharma lineage.
Seeing is not seeing; this is sufficient for the mechanism of the tally. How could dense bamboo ever obstruct the flow of water?
Spring passes and autumn comes; cold and heat distinguish one from the other. There is no need to place a head atop a head.
The seventeenth-generation master, Ying’an Tanhua Chanshi, was a son of the Jiang family of Qizhou. From birth, he was extraordinary and outstanding. He emerged...

He traveled extensively throughout various regions and subsequently visited Huqiu, where he served for one year and suddenly attained enlightenment regarding the Great Matter. He later emerged as the abbot of Tiantong in Mingzhou.
On the anniversary of Huqiu’s death, he offered incense and said: "Throughout my life, I have had no luck; I ran straight into this witless old monk.
Though I exhausted every skill and artifice, I could never find a way to settle with him. From that moment on, I laid down my weapons and put on robes according to my lot."
"Eating a meal. For twenty years he has sat upon a curved wooden bed, hanging up a sheep’s head while selling dog meat.
What authority does he have? Nevertheless, on this day when incense is burned once a year, it causes people’s regret to deepen for all eternity."
At that time, Dahui was at Mei Yang. A monk arrived there bearing a message; Dahui praised it with great fervor and sent a verse, saying:
"Severing the path atop the first peak of the Golden Wheel, A thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide their traces.

Having received the true news once again this year, It reports that the orthodox lineage of Yangqi is now unobstructed. At that time, Dahui and [Foyan] were both celebrated as the "Two Gates of Ambrosia. He once...

He admonished his disciples, saying: "For members of our lineage of patched-robed monks (nāsōng) to wear straw sandals and reside in a monastery—how could this be anything less than a viper clinging to its den?
On the thirteenth day of the sixth month in the first year of the Longxing era of Emperor Xiaozong of the Song dynasty, he passed away. His stupa was enshrined at the home mountain, Tiantong.
Nine persons succeeded him in the Dharma. [Verse:]
Treading through worn-out straw sandals in search of a kindred spirit, Having traversed mountains and rivers, the path grows ever deeper.
Do not say that a poor child thinks only of old debts; Hanging up a goat to sell a dog brings one loathing from others.
The eighteenth-generation Master Mitan Xianjie was a native of the Zheng clan of Fuzhou. His mother dreamed of an elderly monk entering [her chamber].
He was born into the Śākya clan. From childhood, he was exceptionally gifted and surpassed others. Upon reaching maturity, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
He traveled extensively to consult various spiritual teachers. Finally, he visited Ying’an Hua at Mingguo in Quzhou. One day, he asked: "What is the True Dharma Eye?"
He replied, "A broken sand bowl. Ying'an nodded in approval. Thereupon, he took his leave to visit his parents. Ying'an sent him off with a verse, saying:
"The phrase that penetrates the great awakening, Directly opens up the crown of the head. We have followed you for four years now; Your inquiries have left no trace behind.
Though the dharma-bag has not yet been entrusted to you, Your spirit already swallows heaven and earth. Yet you take the Eye of the True Dharma And call it a 'broken sand bowl. Go on this journey..."
As you prepare to pay your respects at court, do not simply evade or follow along. I have a final word; when you return, I require that you abide by it.
Later, he went forth to reside at Kai-fa in Quzhou, and subsequently moved to Xiangfu, Jiangshan, and Huazang. Before long, he received an imperial decree to reside at Jingshan and Lingyin.
He was the Dharma heir of Shiren. (Verse follows).
The momentum of a thousand mountains halts at the foot of the peak; The voices of ten thousand streams are silently gathered upon the sea.
One might marvel that the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Eye The Patriarch called a broken sandpot.
The Nineteenth Generation Master Pō’ān Zuǎn was a native of the Wáng family from Guǎng’ān. He studied under Jì’ān at Líng...

Yunmen was dividing his seat when a practitioner seeking further instruction asked, "The monkey-child cannot be caught; I pray you, grant me your guidance. The Master said, "What is the use of trying to catch it?
It is like wind blowing over water, naturally forming its own ripples. Ascending the hall, he said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.
Unable to restrain my impatience, I shall provide a way for you all to cast off [delusions]. He took up his staff, struck once, and set it down.
The text below says: "Flowing water silently erodes the rocks by the stream; I urge people to eliminate the difficulties of right and wrong.
The four who inherited the Dharma: Nāga’s Great Samādhi contains the autumn within the sea; The monkey atop the tree attains freedom;
The four seas and five lakes are as level as a mirror; Travelers, do not take the road as your enemy.
The twentieth-generation master, Wuzhun Shifan Chanshi, was the son of the Yang family from Zizhong in Shu.
At the age of nine, he left home to become a monk under Daqin of Yiping. He first visited Fozhao, who asked him, "Where are you from? He replied, "Jianzhou. Fozhao said:
"Did you bring your sword? The Master let out a shout as soon as the words were spoken. Daoyuan said, "This black-headed fellow is making a mess of things.

Later, he studied under Pō’ān at Lingyin Monastery and served as the First Seat. One day, while attending Pō’ān during a stroll by the Stone Cone, a practitioner requested instruction on the "monkey" koan.

As the Master stood nearby, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Subsequently, he received an imperial decree to reside at Mount Jingshan, where he was granted the honorary title: [The text ends here.]
Chan Master Fojian passed away on the fifteenth day of the third month in the Jiyou year of the Chunyu era of the Song dynasty’s Lizong Emperor.
His disciples requested a verse, and the Master took up his brush and wrote: "When coming, empty and desolate; When departing, bare and naked.
If you wish to ask for the ultimate point, Tiantai has its Stone Bridge. His stupa was enshrined at Yuanzhao Monastery. He had seventeen dharma heirs. A verse [in praise]:
Carrying the precious sword of Jianzhou, he arrived; with a single shout at Dangyang, all dust was swept away.
As the evening wind plays the melodies of the Guanshan pipes, the gibbons of the Ba Gorges hear the sound and grieve of their own accord.
The twenty-first generation, Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin, first studied under Tianmu Li, and later under Wuzhun.
He remained in the assembly for many years. Whenever he entered the room [for formal meditation], as soon as the "Master" (the primary subject) was raised, he would leap up with vigor.

Yet, regarding the very core of a true monk or the fangs and claws of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, there was no place for him to apply his teeth. Thus ten years passed. Later, he went to stay at Mount Tianmu in Zhejiang.
One day, while walking in front of the Buddha Hall, his eyes suddenly opened wide; he encountered an ancient tree, and upon touching it—toward... [he broke through].
When the realms thus attained are suddenly cast down all at once, the obstructing mass that has been stifling the chest disperses with a thud;
only then does one begin to see where the Old Man of Jingshan stands. He deserves thirty blows of the staff.

Later, he emerged from seclusion to reside at Longxing Monastery in Tanzhou and finally at Yangshan in Yuanzhou, serving as abbot at six monasteries in total. [This was] presented on the anniversary of Wuzu’s death.
Fragrant Clouds: Everyone says that today the former Master has died; who would have known it was his birthday? What evidence is there for this?
Purple cypress and yellow sandalwood were all suddenly consumed by fire. Eight disciples succeeded to the Dharma. [Their] verses follow.
When the monk’s nostrils suddenly lift their gaze, they strike against a single tree in the courtyard;
if you wish to see where Jingshan stands firm, thirty blows of the black staff will leave his mouth agape.
The twenty-second generation master, Gaofeng Yuanmiao, was the son of the Xu family of Wujiang. His mother dreamed of a monk entering [her womb].

She conceived while still pregnant and gave birth in the Wuxu year of Emperor Lizong’s reign of the Song dynasty. Upon entering the monastic life, she first visited Duanqiao Lun, and subsequently studied under Xueyan.
As soon as she would inquire after him, she was struck out; later, whenever she entered his door, Xueyan would immediately ask, "Who brought this corpse here for you to drag?
and he would strike her out again. This happened countless times. One day, on the anniversary of Shaolin’s memorial service, she followed [him].
The assembly went to the Three Pagodas. While chanting the sutras, one of them suddenly raised his head and beheld the eulogy for the Fifth Patriarch, which read:
"In three hundred and sixty thousand days of a hundred-year life, it is always this very man who turns back and forth. At that moment, he suddenly shattered his doubts.
One day, Yanguan asked him, "During the vast activity of the daytime, can you maintain mastery? He replied, "I can maintain mastery. Yanguan said, "What about in the midst of sleep and dreams?"
"Can you act as the master? He replied, "I can act as the master. Yankou said, "When you are fast asleep, with no dreams and no thoughts, no seeing and no hearing—where is the master then?
The Master had no reply. Thereupon, he resolved to enter Longxu, vowing to himself: "I shall risk spending a lifetime as a simpleton;
I must by all means clarify this one point. After five years, because of a fellow practitioner...

As the monk pushed the pillow, it fell to the ground with a sound. In that moment, he attained great and vast enlightenment. He said to himself: "It is like seeing the Great Sage at Sizhou; like a traveler returning to his native village.
Originally, I am just the person I was before; I have not changed my former way of walking. From this point on, he brought peace to the realm and established order in the land;
all under heaven enjoyed tranquility. With a single thought of non-action, he cut off the ten directions. He went forth to reside at Shuanglin.
Jitiānmù (Huitianmu) entered nirvana on the first day of the twelfth month of the year Yǐwèi (1295) during the Yuánzhēn era of Emperor Chéngzōng of the Great Yuan.
He had four successors in the Dharma lineage. Verse:
"Who is it that drags this corpse here? In dreams and thoughts alike, there is nothing—yet it is buried alive once more.
Suddenly, the pillow falls crashing to the ground; How lamentable! At the Snowy Ridge, one sighs at this marvel!
The twenty-third patriarch, Chan Master Mingben of Mount Zhongfeng, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou. His secular surname was Sun. His mother...
The Li family had a dream in which a gateless path was opened and a wayfarer carrying a lantern arrived at their home; thus, the Master was born. At the age of nine, he lost his mother;
at fifteen, he went to Gaofeng to receive the tonsure. At twenty-four, while observing the flow [of the mind], he attained a realization. He then went to Gaofeng to seek verification.
Feng drove him out with a blow. Because of this, the people spread a rumor that the authorities were selecting young boys and girls.
The Master asked, "If someone were to come and ask the Master for a young boy or girl, what would you do? Feng replied, "I would simply hand him a bamboo staff.
At these words, the Master attained a clear and thorough realization of the source of the Dharma. Feng wrote a portrait eulogy and gave it to the Master, saying, "My appearance is inconceivable."
[The assembly] deliberated: "Neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs could perceive it; only this unworthy child has been granted the sight of half his nose.
Furthermore, he permitted his disciples to approach the Master to seek further instruction. Consequently, students flocked to him from all directions like water flowing downward.

Yet the Master remained humble and concealed, never once being willing to assume the position of a teacher. At that time, the Son of Heaven and the high officials would always leave the seat of honor vacant at Mount Jing for him.
The various great monasteries of Lingyin invited the Master to reside there. He was granted the title "Buddha-Love Perfectly Illuminating Vast Wisdom" (Fuci Yuanzhao Guanghui).
He passed away on the fourteenth day of the eighth month in the third year of the Zhizhi era of the Great Yuan Emperor Yingzong.
His posthumous title was "Puying" (Universal Response). The following is a verse by his dharma successor:
The source flows surging eastward; the sea is vast and the heavens high, where all phenomena merge.
When the bamboo whisk is taken up, the whole body is revealed; within a single hair-tip, the fundamental principle is settled.
The twenty-fourth generation master, Chan Master Qianyan Yuanzhang, was a son of the Dong family of Xiaoshan. He initially pursued the study of Confucianism. At the age of...
At seventeen, he mastered the teachings of the hundred schools; at nineteen, he left the dust of the world to receive full ordination. He studied the Vinaya in Wulin.

During a vegetarian feast for the Sangha held at the Chancellor’s residence, the Master joined the assembly to receive offerings. At that time, Zhongfeng was already seated among them; upon seeing the Master, he called out, "How do you conduct your daily practice?
The Master replied, "I recite the Buddha's name. Zhongfeng asked, "Where is the Buddha now? As the Master hesitated, Zhongfeng raised his voice sharply:
He rebuked him. The Master requested instruction, and Feng gave him the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature to investigate.

Thereupon, he bound up some thatched grass in the midst of Mount Lingyin. Suddenly, after ten years had passed, while visiting Wangzhou Pavilion, he heard the sound of sparrows and attained realization.
He went to see Feng, who again rebuked him. The Master was indignant and remained undeluded. One night at midnight, a mouse overturned a cat’s food bowl, causing it to fall to the ground.
He made a sound, and suddenly attained awakening. He felt his body leap up several *zhang*. He went to consult Master Feng, who asked, "For what reason did Zhaozhou say 'no'?
The Master replied, "A rat ate the cat's meal. Feng said, "Not yet. The Master said, "The vessel was broken.
Feng asked, "What happened after it was broken? The Master said, "It shattered against the square bricks. Feng then smiled slightly and instructed him, saying, "You should..."

Guard yourself well. Retire to dwell among the crags and caves; when the time arrives, the principle will manifest of itself. Having received this entrustment, he then withdrew to the Eastern Hermitage of Tianlong, where his reputation and radiance grew daily more prominent.
By imperial decree, he was summoned to reside at Shengshou Monastery, granted the title Yuanjian (Perfect Mirror), and presented with a golden brocade dharma robe.
He passed away in the sixth month of the Dingyou year of the Zhizheng era under Emperor Shunzong of the Great Yuan. His verse says: "Level..."

Born with a garrulous tongue, today you have met your downfall. One phrase roars through the heavens; the Eye of the True Dharma is extinguished. To the four who succeeded the Dharma, they offer this verse:
The cat’s bowl is overturned, not a speck of dust remains; Before the sound, suddenly the smile upon the face unfolds.
Zhaozhou’s dog lies sleeping in the middle of the road; Passersby on the path can no longer pass to and fro.

The twenty-fifth patriarch, Chan Master Wanfeng Shiwei, was the son of the Jin family of Wenzhou. His mother, surnamed Zheng, dreamed that two figures—one Confucian and one Buddhist—entered her chamber;

His paternal aunt took him in and nurtured him. While still in his swaddling clothes, he saw a monk and smiled. When he grew up, he relied upon a lecture master.
Master Sheng received full ordination and left the household life. He went to visit the elder Qianyan, who asked him, "With what do you come to meet this old monk?
The Master raised his fist and said, "I meet the Abbot right here. Qianyan said, "Once dead and burned, where will you establish yourself and find your livelihood?
The Master replied, "The bubble arises and the bubble perishes, yet the water remains; when the wind ceases and the waves subside, the moon is reflected."
Tanhui asked, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing—what is it? The Master drew a circle with his sitting mat and stood with his hands folded.
One day, while they were working together to cut pine trees, the Master picked up a round stone and made the gesture of offering a pearl, saying, "I ask the Master to appraise its value.
Tanhui said, "It is not worth half a coin. The Master said, "Blind! Tanhui said, "I am also blind."
