Lush yellow flowers fill the eyes; autumn is here. Baizhang sits upright atop a green peak.

Lightly bringing forth the phrase of "no guest or host," A single shout makes the waters of a thousand rivers flow backward. The Master presented this verse: Nanquan did not intend to vex people's minds;
Some wish to use the mind to grasp the mind. This is neither my mind nor a Buddha; In the vast expanse of the sky-like nature, what is there to seek?
Yan agreed. Before long, he went into seclusion; when Yan summoned him, he did not go, instead entrusting him with his dharma robes and the image of his crown protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*).
Later, he planted his staff at Mount Dengwei in Suzhou, where his monastic community flourished greatly.

On the twenty-ninth day of the first month of the fourteenth year of the Hongwu era of the Great Ming (the *xinyou* year), he demonstrated his entry into *nirvāṇa*. Thirteen people succeeded him in the Dharma. [Verse:]
An extraordinary spirit, a poverty that pierces to the bone; Raising one’s fist as a gesture of human feeling.
Where teacher and student find perfect accord like a needle and its eye, A single shout clearly establishes host and guest.
The twenty-sixth generation, Chan Master Baozang Puchi, long relied upon Wanfeng. The verse of dharma transmission says: Great...

The fool suffers pain beneath the ribs and clenches his fists. The Three Essentials and Three Mysteries transcend both the orthodox and the biased. Within the cave of Linji, the lion’s cubs continue the lineage;
lamp after lamp transmits the flame through ancient and modern times. He succeeded to the abbacy of Sheng’en as its second patriarch. There were three who inherited the Dharma from him. A verse:
The Great Fool’s ribs transmitted the message; the Huatuo lineage spread and the true pulse grew long.
Sitting amidst white clouds was ultimately not the ultimate; moving the boat allows for a different deliberation.
The twenty-seventh generation, Chan Master Dongming Huida, was the son of the Wang family of Danyang. At the age of fourteen, he relied upon [a master].
Zhanran shaved his head and received full ordination. While emerging from meditative concentration, he attained realization while gazing at a pine tree;

subsequently, he presented his awakening to Baozang, who rebuked him. Thereupon, he attended closely under Baozang’s guidance. One day, Baozang asked, "The mind is not the Buddha, and wisdom is not the Way. How do you understand this?
The Master stepped forward to pay his respects and stood with his hands joined in *añjali*. Baozang scolded him, saying, "You have been here for so long..."

At that time, he returned with this kind of understanding. The Master then became indignant. On the third day, [the student] suddenly reached the very bottom of the Dharma source and presented a verse, saying:
"A single punch shatters the vast void; The billions of Sumeru mountains leave no trace.
If one asks who is the master within this, A single red orb surges forth from the Eastern Sea. [The Master] gave him a secret instruction, saying: "Guard and uphold it well yourself. Great!

On the final day of the sixth month in the Xinde year of the Ming dynasty (the Xin-you year), he passed away. Following the cremation, countless *śarīra* relics were found. He had two successors in the Dharma lineage. Verse:
The Buddha-mind, wisdom, and the Way all rest at once; When pressed against the void, one knows how to turn the head.
A *jizi* (atom) containing ten billion Mount Sumerus; a single autumnal moon surges forth from the Fusang tree.
The twenty-eighth generation master, Chan Master Haizhou Puci, was a native of the Qian clan of Changshu in Suzhou. His family had followed the Confucian profession for generations.
He left the household life to study the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. Upon reaching the passage that states, "Where there are only words and explanations, there is no real meaning," he said:
"Discourse has become increasingly abundant today," he said. He then returned to seek the true meaning (*tattvārtha*). Upon arriving at Wanfeng, he raised the question.
Wanfeng stamped the ground twice with his feet and said, "This very thing is the true meaning. The Master had an awakening and remarked, "The Master has exerted too much effort for my sake."

Feng smiled and granted his request. He then built a hermitage in a valley of Mount Dongting. After twenty years, because a monk criticized his understanding, he abandoned the hermitage and went to visit Dongming.
Dongming asked, "Have you ever met anyone? The Master replied, "If I were to speak of it, I fear it would startle people.
Dongming said, "Even if you had personally met Śākyamuni, you would still be just an ordinary fellow. Why not just say it?"
The Master said, "Wanfeng. Ming asked, "Where is Wanfeng right now? The Master’s face turned crimson with embarrassment. Ming said, "If it is like this, you have never seen Wanfeng.
The Master returned to his quarters and for three days and nights forgot both sleep and food. By chance, the cord of the incense lamp snapped and fell to the ground;
at that moment, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. He went before the gate to present the account of his realization. Ming said, "Old..."
"Ācārya, you have inherited the lineage from Wanfeng," [the Master] said. "Since you have now been thoroughly penetrated by me, how can you claim to inherit from Wanfeng?
Ming then left the mountain pass and ascended the seat, saying: "Gautama had no intention for whom to transmit; Kāśyapa’s smile was groundless.
Reaching this point, even the Seven Buddhas cannot prevail; Mañjuśrī’s flushed face is in vain. Today is a fine occasion for laughter."
The matter of Dongmyeong has caused people to waste their spittle and drool for a thousand ages. Fortunately, Master Haengwang forgot both self and other;

thus, a single stream of the Je lineage continues unceasingly. [He] threw down his staff and said: "The burden of a thousand catties is now fully entrusted [to you]. The profound and the essential are now discussed by this staff.
[He] struck three times with the whisk and descended from the seat. Not long after, Dongmyeong passed away, and the assembly requested [him] to succeed to the seat.

On the anniversary of the death of Wanfeng, he held up the incense and gave two shouts, saying: "I simply laugh at you, a headless teacher who protects your own shortcomings and treats the Buddha-dharma as mere social obligation.
He then prostrated. Again holding up the incense, he said: "This ball of incense is offered to the Elder Dongming.
With a single heart of sincerity, he spurred me on, causing me to penetrate the source of the lineage. He then gave two shouts. "Where the debt of gratitude is deep, one must act accordingly."
At home, it is only when there is milk that one knows it is one’s mother. He prostrated himself and wept bitterly; then he returned to his quarters.
As he approached the time of his passing, he spoke this verse: "Ninety-six years spent in the world, Seventy-four years as a monk. How much confusion and error lay within!"
Upon seeing this, Dongming passed away. [The Master] struck a circle with his whisk and said, "From Śākyamuni until my sixty-second generation, there have been countless old *ho-shangs*.
[He struck another circle and said,] 'Mostly they find their resting place here. *Tu!* Then he threw down his brush and passed away. This was in the first year of the Jingtai era.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa to the left of Dongming. He had received the Dharma from ten masters."
Two Verses: When nine fathoms are nearly completed, the lofty peak soars high; Only when the final basketful is added does the merit become manifest.
From this point on, deep gratitude finds its place; A thousand streams and ten thousand branches all flow toward the East.
The twenty-ninth patriarch, Chan Master Baofeng Mingxuan, was the son of the Fan family of Wujiang, Suzhou. By secular profession, he was a carpenter.

While assisting Haizhou in constructing a pagoda, he injured his foot so severely that it caused him intense pain. He asked for wine to drink, whereupon Haizhou said to him, "Fortunately, you have only injured your foot;
had I cut off your head, would you still be able to drink? At these words, he attained enlightenment and subsequently requested ordination, serving as the monastery’s cook.
One day, while carrying firewood on his head, Tou was seen by Master Zhou, who asked, "What are you doing with these thorns?

Tou replied, "They are firewood. Zhou let out a great laugh. Tou was bewildered. Zhou said, "If they are firewood, take them away and burn them. Tou rose and asked with doubt, "Ultimately, what is the principle here?
Zhou did not answer. That night, he applied himself with intense effort to investigate this, until he was suddenly struck by a flash of insight.
His eyebrows were gone; his face looked as if it had been sliced with a knife. When he looked into a mirror, he attained sudden and great enlightenment.
He presented this realization to Master Zhōu, who then struck him. The Master snatched the staff away and said, "This six-foot pole has not been used for many years;
today you have taken it up again. Zhōu laughed heartily. The Master offered this verse: "Where the staff strikes, blood stains appear; Within the laughter, a blade is hidden."
"Look closely! If one is a true man of heroic spirit, even a dead man will mumble when struck with a staff. Zhou said, "By these very verses, you may succeed to my school.
He then bestowed the verse upon him, saying: "The descendants of Linji are lions; A single roar sends a thousand mountains echoing, and the hundred beasts die.
Today you possess the majesty of claws and fangs, Yet you must still hide deep within the ten thousand ravines. From... (The text continues from here.)
His fame spread far and wide, and students gathered like clouds. On the ninth day of the twelfth month in the eighth year of the Chenghua era, he manifested parinirvāṇa.
His stūpa was erected to the left of Dongming Temple. Five people succeeded him in the Dharma. [Verse:]
Tumbling eastward and leaning westward, the tripod legs have broken; Only one with a sincere heart can uphold it.
Though fire burns and blades slice away every hair on his brow, Before the Mirror of Karma, his true nature is revealed.
The thirtieth generation: Chan Master Tianqi Benrui of Nanchang. Born into the Jiang family of Zhongling, he was twenty years old [when he entered the path].
He followed his father on a merchant journey to Yingzhou. Having become weary of worldly phenomena, he received the tonsure from Master Wushuo Neng and was instructed to contemplate the phrase:
"All dharmas return to One; to what does the One return? He then visited senior masters and investigated this day and night, gradually attaining moments of awakening.
Finally, he went to visit Master Bao. Master Feng asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Beijing.
Master Feng said, "Are you still only in Beijing, or have you gone elsewhere? The Master said, "I am carefree wherever I am. Master Feng asked, "Have you ever been to Sichuan? He replied, "I have.
Master Feng asked, "How is the landscape of Sichuan compared to here? He said, "Though the mountains and rivers differ, the wind and moon are one."
Yunyan Ban raised his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this? He replied, "No. Yunyan asked, "Why then is it not there?
The Master said, "It is not within my realm. Yunyan asked, "What then is your realm? He replied, "Even all Buddhas cannot recognize it."
"Who dares to forcibly impose a name upon you? Fēng said, "Are you not yourself clinging to emptiness? He replied, "I will never make my livelihood within a ghost cave.
Fēng said, "Among the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths in the Western Heaven, you are the foremost. The Master shook his sleeves and departed. He then bestowed this verse:
"Jìshān’s staff and shouts can be lightly touched; From of old, his hands and eyes have been clear in killing and giving life."
The noble understanding and ordinary sentiments are both severed at once; A fresh branch of the *dharma-puṣpa* still blooms anew. Thirty-nine persons succeeded to the Dharma.
Though the names of mountains and rivers and their historical traces differ, The principle of wind and moon has always been the same.
When the birds are exhausted, the bow is hidden; when the campaign ends, The Ten-Thousand-Chariot Sovereign sits with folded hands within the realm.
The thirty-first generation was Chan Master Wencong of Xuewen, a native of the Xi family from Guanzhe County in Shaowu.

When the Master was three years old, both his parents passed away; his maternal grandfather took pity on him and raised him. At seventeen, he received the tonsure, and at twenty, he received full ordination.
He applied himself diligently to the study of the *Vinaya*, *Samatha-vipaśyanā*, and the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* and other treatises. One day, while traveling to Baiyang Mountain, he encountered...

How can this principle be explained? The Master then lectured on it according to the literal text. The elderly practitioner reviled him and departed.
From this point on, the Master gave rise to a state of intense doubt (*yiqing*). He applied himself with diligence, moment after moment, for five or six years.

He resided at Guanziling in Suizhou, where he transmitted the Dharma to five people. His verse:
The woodcutter returns home to find the chess pieces rotted away; the fisherman reaches the shore and desists from asking for the ford.
Holy understanding and mundane sentiment are both cut off at their root. This is the original face.
At Stone Fragrance Pavilion, the thirty-second generation, Chan Master Xiaoyan Debao, was born to the Wu family of Jintai. His lineage was that of the Jin-yi (Silk-Robed) nobility.

I traveled extensively to visit renowned masters, experiencing everything from the fire-places of Mount Fu-niu to the *śamatha-vipaśyanā* of the Pure Land school.

The thirty-third generation successor, Chan Master Huanyou Zhengzhuan, was the son of the Lü family of Liyang.

At the age of nineteen, he received the tonsure under Master Lè’ān, who instructed him to contemplate the koan of "the state before one's parents were born. After a long time without realization, he applied himself with diligent effort.
After more than two weeks had passed, he suddenly attained awakening upon hearing the sound of a lamp-flower bursting. He then proceeded directly to Yan.
The Master went to visit Master Xiangyan to seek verification of his realization. Xiangyan said, "Tell me everything about how you have attained strength from the past, one by one.
The Master answered truthfully. In the midst of their conversation, Xiangyan suddenly kicked out his shoe and said, "Speak a single word here!
He then cut off the thread of the discussion all at once. The Master could not sleep the entire night; by the following morning, he was still standing beneath the eaves.

Yanxian came out from his cave to call him. The Master turned his head, whereupon Yanxian raised one foot, assuming the posture of an asura obstructing the sun and moon. At that moment, the Master experienced a sudden and profound liberation.
He served Yanxian diligently for several years before taking his leave to return south. Yanxian wrote a letter entrusting him with the lineage transmitted from his predecessors.
As he was about to depart, [his teacher] presented him with a single straw hat and said, "Do not let your sharp edges show.
The Master first resided at Longchi, then moved to Wutai and Beijing Puzhao, and later returned once more to Longchi. There, he inscribed a verse on an incense burner which says:
"With ears to hear sounds, yet as if deaf; No room for other things to stir within. The extinguishing of the mind may not always be thus, But winning this pure smoke is enough."

These were different. Furthermore, fearing that students might fall into the extremes of nihilism or eternalism, he composed three treatises: *Bōgo* (Refuting Errors), *Shōjūshaku* (Explanation of the Abiding Nature), and *Motsu-fukō* (Things Do Not Shift).
These were carved into woodblocks and circulated in the world. He passed away in the second month of spring in the Jia-yin year of the Wanli era and was interred at his home mountain.
There were four successors to his Dharma: Tiantong Wu, Qingshan Xiu, Jingming Lian, and Jingshan Xin. Under Qingshan...

The thirty-fourth patriarch, Chan Master Míyún Yuánwù of Tiāntóng, was the son of the Jiǎng family of Yíxīng. His family was poor, and he made his living by gathering firewood.
At the age of twenty-seven, while carrying a load across a mountain bend, he had an awakening upon touching a pile of firewood by the roadside.
He then left the household life under the guidance of Master Huanyou. He constantly reflected that the arrival of birth and death was ultimately unstable.

Throughout the twenty-four hours of the day and night, he observed that mind and phenomena stood as two separate entities. He recalled the words of the ancients: "Heaven and earth share the same root; the myriad things are one body."
The more he looked, the more it appeared as two distinct things. He requested instruction from Longchi, who said, "If you reach such a state, simply let go of yourself and lie down.
Thereafter, [Longchi] did nothing but scold him. The Master was overcome by a mixture of shame and despondency, so he retreated behind closed doors for several years.
It happened that Master Quan entered the capital and appointed the Master to oversee the affairs of the monastery. One day, returning from the city, he passed over the summit of Tongguan Mountain.
Suddenly, he realized that the sentient and the insentient appeared with a brilliant, equal clarity; not even a hair’s breadth of fault or affliction could be found.
For the most part, it cannot be described to others. This is precisely what is called the state where the great earth sinks level.
He then went to visit Huan. Huan asked, "Do you have any new realization? The Master said, "When one person rejoices, the myriad people enjoy their labors. Huan said, "You..."
Again, [Dongshan] asked, "How about this? Yunyan said, "I have come to pay my respects to you, Master. Yunyan said, "Thinking of how far you have traveled, I shall let you off with thirty blows.
Dongshan then withdrew his body and departed. One day, Yunyan asked, "If someone were to suddenly question you, how would you respond?
Dongshan abruptly held up his fist. Yunyan said, "I do not understand; what does this mean? Dongshan... [remained silent].
He said, "Do not say that the Master does not understand; even the Buddhas of the three periods do not understand.
On another day, Huan raised his whisk and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in other quarters? The Master let out a thunderous shout. Huan said, "What a fine shout!
The Master shouted twice more and returned to his place. One day, Longchi called for him, and when Jueyu entered the room, he said:
The old monk has risen in the night and gone out once more; the handle is now entirely in my hands. You all must support the Buddha-dharma for me.
The Master then presented a verse, saying: "If I, this fellow, were to support the Buddha-dharma, I would give thirty blows to him regardless of what he does—whether he be right or wrong.
Do not say that I am being clear about rewards and punishments. Longchi observed this.

Da Xiao passed away shortly thereafter. The Master remained at his stupa for three years. In the Ding-si year of the Wanli era, the assembly requested that he succeed to the seat and propagate the Dharma.
Subsequently, he resided at six great monasteries: Tongxuan, Jinsu, Huangbo, Yuwang, and Tiantong. His school’s influence flourished greatly.
On the seventh day of the seventh month in the Ren-wu year of the Chongzhen era (1642), he suddenly passed away while sitting in meditation; his radiance illuminated the night.

The four surrounding mountains turned white. He lived to the age of seventy-seven. Tongxuan escorted his entire remains back, where they were enshrined in a stupa on the right ridge of the Huanzhu Hermitage at Tiantong.
Twelve people succeeded him in the Dharma: Wufeng Xue, Han Yue Cang, and Poshan Ming.
